newsitem.title: USA: Investment Grade sees inflation as threat.
newsitem.headline: Investment Grade sees inflation as threat.

text.p: Investment Grade Municipal Income Fund Inc said Friday "the wildcard of inflation is still a potential threat" to the municipal bond market.
The fund, which invests in long-term municipal obligations, also said growth in new issues and refunding in the face of an rallying market could stall municipal bonds.

The fund's top five sectors as of July 31 were: Water (17.8 percent), power (17.1), general obligations (11.6), health care (11.0) and sales tax (7.4) spread over New York (14.5 percent), Texas (12.6), Illinois (12.4), Indiana (11.1) and Massachusetts (7.4).
The fund's portfolio was made up of AAA bonds (44.7 percent), AA bonds (29.2), A bonds (15.4), BBB bonds (6.6) and cash (4.1).
The bonds' weighted maturity averaged 18.42 years and the weighted duration 4.32 years. The weighted coupon averaged 6.34 percent and the AMT paper 0 percent.
